Daily Brief

The day after Tuesday's US midterm elections, the political fallout continues to dominate headlines as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress in January, marking a significant rebuke of President Trump's administration [BBC, RFI, The Hindu]. Vice President JD Vance issued a striking public critique blaming the Iran war for Republican losses, widely seen as positioning for a 2028 presidential run [BBC]. In France, a major day of nationwide strikes brought hundreds of thousands to the streets demanding higher wages and better public services, with 70,000 police deployed amid concerns about potential violence [BBC, RFI, Al Jazeera]. Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong received a 10-year prison sentence under the national security law, adding to his existing detention and drawing international attention to Beijing's ongoing crackdown on dissent [BBC, Le Monde]. In Israel, coalition negotiations intensified as former military chief Gadi Eisenkot emerged as the frontrunner to form a government after an ultra-Orthodox party declined to recommend Prime Minister Netanyahu [The Hindu]. Meanwhile, European aviation authorities grappled with a third consecutive day of bomb threats affecting dozens of flights, all of which have so far proven to be hoaxes [BBC, ABC Australia, France 24].

Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Sentenced to 10 Years Under National Security Law

  • Wong, 30, was sentenced for 'colluding with foreign forces' under Hong Kong's 2020 national security law
  • Having already served six years in prison, he was due for release in January but will now remain imprisoned until 2036
  • Wong has been arrested multiple times since beginning his activism as a teenager and was once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement
  • Critics say the law has silenced dissent; authorities maintain it is needed for stability

  • Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot positioned to receive mandate to form government after October 27 election ended in deadlock
